Blend points or another graph into a street network

Source: R/blend.R
ox_blend.Rd

Snaps point locations onto their nearest network edge and splits that edge there, turning each snapped location into a routable node — the osmnxr counterpart of sfnetworks::st_network_blend(), with the snapping done in the Rust core (grid-indexed planar distance) so city-sized networks blend in seconds.

Usage

ox_blend(
  g,
  y,
  tolerance = Inf,
  connector_attrs = list(),
  snap_nodes = TRUE,
  snap_edges = TRUE,
  connector_node_attrs = character()
)

Arguments

g

An osm_graph to blend into.

y

What to blend: an sf/sfc of POINT geometries, or another osm_graph (same CRS as g). Attribute columns of an sf y are carried onto the new nodes they create.

tolerance

Maximum snapping distance, in CRS units. Points (or y nodes) farther than this from every edge of g are not blended. Default Inf.

connector_attrs

Named list of constant attribute values for the connector edges created in graph mode (e.g. list(highway = "connector", travel_time = 60)). Columns the connectors do not set are NA-filled — in particular, set travel_time here (or fix it afterwards) before routing the blended graph on travel time. Ignored when y is a set of points.

snap_nodes

Which points (or y nodes) may be snapped: TRUE (the default, all of them) or a logical vector with one flag per point / y node. Flagged-off points get an NA row in meta$blend; in graph mode, flagged-off y nodes still enter the union with y's own edges — they just get no connector (e.g. a station's street-level gates snap, its platforms don't and are reached through the gates).

snap_edges

Which edges of g may receive snapped points: TRUE (the default, all of them) or a logical vector with one flag per row of g$edges (e.g. rule out limited-access flyovers that pass close by). Note the flag governs where points may land, not split propagation: when a snapped edge is split, edges sharing its geometry (the reversed twin of a two-way street) are split with it regardless of their own flag, to keep both directions routable.

connector_node_attrs

Character vector of y node attribute columns to copy onto the two connector edges of each snapped y node in graph mode (e.g. a per-station access time that should weight the connector). Errors when a column is absent from y's nodes or clashes with connector_attrs or a connector-reserved column (u, v, length). Ignored when y is a set of points.

Value

An osm_graph. meta$blend records the mapping as a tibble: one row per input point (or y node not shared with g), with the node osmid it became or attached to (NA when beyond tolerance or flagged off by snap_nodes), the snapping distance, and u / v — the endpoints of the g edge it snapped onto, as that edge was before the blend (splitting replaces it with pieces chained through the new nodes).

Details

Two-way streets are handled properly: every edge sharing the split edge's geometry (its reversed twin, or a same-direction duplicate) is split at the same location into the same new node, so routability is preserved in both directions. Points that project onto an existing node are attached to that node instead of splitting. Points farther than tolerance from every edge are left out with a warning. New nodes get consecutive osmids starting just above the largest id in sight (g's — and y's too in graph mode), so existing ids keep their meaning.

When y is another osm_graph, the result is a combined multimodal network, built in three steps (as proposed in the issue that motivated this feature): (1) every node of y (within tolerance, and flagged by snap_nodes) is blended into g as above; (2) the two graphs are stacked with ox_union(), so y's own nodes and edges are kept intact; (3) a pair of directed connector edges is added between each y node and the node it snapped to, which is the connectivity a plain blend + union would miss. Node osmids shared by both graphs are merged by the union directly (no connector needed) — but only when they sit at the same coordinates: reusing an id of g for a genuinely different location in y is an error (renumber y's ids first). The union here does not deduplicate edges (the two layers are assumed to be distinct networks); combine overlapping downloads with ox_union() first when that matters.

Distances are planar, in the units of the graph's CRS (reproject geographic networks first — sf::st_transform() on nodes and edges — when a metric tolerance matters). Split edges keep their attributes; length is recomputed from the new geometries, and travel_time / penalty (when present) are rescaled proportionally to each piece's share of the parent edge, so routing weights stay consistent.

Examples

g <- example_osm_graph()

# blend two POIs into the grid: each becomes a routable node
pts <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(150, 40)), sf::st_point(c(250, 260)),
                  crs = 3857)
b <- ox_blend(g, pts)
b$meta$blend
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   point  node  dist     u     v
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1    17    40     5     9
#> 2     2    18    40    12    16
ox_shortest_path(b, b$meta$blend$node[1], b$meta$blend$node[2])
#> [1] 17  9 10 11 12 18

# blend a tiny second network (e.g. a metro line) into the grid
metro <- new_osm_graph(
  sf::st_sf(osmid = c(1001, 1002), access_time = c(30, 45),
            geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(40, 150)),
                                  sf::st_point(c(260, 150)), crs = 3857)),
  sf::st_sf(u = 1001, v = 1002, length = 220,
            geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_linestring(
              rbind(c(40, 150), c(260, 150))), crs = 3857)),
  meta = list(network_type = "metro")
)
mm <- ox_blend(g, metro, connector_attrs = list(highway = "connector"),
               connector_node_attrs = "access_time")
mm
#> 
#> ── osm_graph ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 20 nodes, 57 edges
#> Network type: "drive+metro"
#> Simplified: FALSE
#> CRS: "EPSG:3857"
